title: Azerbaijani — Cyrillic (1958–1991) to official Latin alphabet
authority: Law on the restoration of the Latin-based Azerbaijani alphabet (25 Dec 1991), alphabet revised 1992; letter correspondence as in BGN/PCGN 1993
description: Converts legacy Soviet Azerbaijani Cyrillic (superseded in 1991/1992) to today's official Latin alphabet: Ә→Ə, Г→Q, Ҝ→G, Ғ→Ğ, Ј→Y, Ҹ→C, Ч→Ç, Ж→J, Х→X, Һ→H, Ы→I/ı, И→İ/i, Ө→Ö, Ү→Ü, Ш→Ş.
notes: The source script is superseded (Cyrillic was used 1939–1991); the target alphabet is the current official one, so this scheme is the standard way to bring Soviet-era records into today's spelling.
Ј is U+0408/U+0458 (it looks like Latin J but means y). Г is the voiced uvular q, К is k, Ҝ is the palatal g.
Obsolete pre-1958 letters й, э, ю, я are rendered y, e, yu, ya (PCGN uses ẏ, ė, yu, ya).
Russian-form spellings in Soviet documents (Алиев, Мамедов, Гусейнов) are Russian, not Azerbaijani Cyrillic; this table turns them into Aliev, Mamedov, Quseynov. Use a Russian scheme for such names.

Python upper-cases i to I, but Azerbaijani capital i is İ (U+0130) and I is the capital of ı. И is therefore emitted as a placeholder (U+0269/U+0196) that a post rule turns into i/İ, so Имишли → İmişli and ИЛҺАМ → İLHAM.
